memos.label: Kennel Card / Bio
memos.text: Hi there, I’m Achilles, and I’ve got a heart as big as my name! If you’re looking for a loyal adventure buddy, I might just be your guy. I absolutely love going on walks, exploring new places, and soaking up all the sights and smells along the way. Whether it’s a stroll around the neighborhood or a fun outing, I’m always ready to be right by your side. I’m also a pretty social pup, I get along well with other dogs and enjoy having friends around. When I’m not out adventuring, you can usually find me playing with my toys or happily hanging out, soaking up all the love I can get. I’ve got a fun, sweet personality and I’m always ready to bring some joy into your day. I’m currently looking for someone who’s ready to make me part of their life and I promise to return the favor with endless love and companionship. Achilles will be transported to the Shelter Pet Adoption Center located inside Petco at 10017 Biddick Lane Huntersville, NC 28078 on May 8th, 2026 if he has a committed foster or adopter. If you are interested in fostering or adopting Achilles, please email NCteam@austinpetsalive.org or call 704-266-3647.

memos.label: Disclaimer
memos.text: This Addendum supplements your Adoption Contract with Austin Pets Alive! and outlines your obligations regarding the spay/neuter of your adopted pet. 1. Veterinary Care and Spay/Neuter Requirement I understand and agree to the following: (a) If my puppy has been released to me before being spayed or neutered, I agree to have the surgery completed within 90 days of the adoption date (b) I will follow veterinary guidelines to ensure my pet is fully vaccinated and protected from common diseases. (c) I understand that I am responsible for managing, training, and socializing my pet to develop appropriate behavior. 2. Spay/Neuter Scheduling Options Within two weeks of adoption, Shelter Pet Adoption Center staff will contact me by phone or email to schedule a spay/neuter appointment with one of Austin Pets Alive!’s veterinary partners. (a) If I choose this option, Austin Pets Alive! will cover the cost of the surgery and required medications directly related to that procedure. (b) I understand that any additional services (vaccinations, elective procedures, or other treatments) will be my financial responsibility. (c) Post-surgery complications due to non-compliance as decided by Austin Pets Alive! will be my responsibility 3. Using a Private Veterinarian I may choose to schedule the surgery with my own licensed veterinarian. In that case, I am responsible for all related costs. Proof of spay/neuter (such as a veterinary invoice or certificate) must be submitted to NCteam@austinpetsalive.org within 90 days of adoption. 4. Compliance Failure to provide proof of spay/neuter within 90 days may result in follow-up contact from Austin Pets Alive! and may be considered a breach of the adoption contract. A Friendly Note: You are not required to use your own vet, but doing so helps stretch our limited nonprofit resources and allows us to save more pets in need. Every time an adopter covers this cost, it helps us reach another animal waiting for help. Adopter Acknowledgment By signing the adoption contract, I acknowledge that I have read, understand, and agree to the terms of this Spay/Neuter Addendum.

memos.label: Kennel Card / Bio
memos.text: Hi, I’m Alex! I’m a 5-month-old girl kitten, and I’m a little shy when we first meet. New people and new places can feel a bit overwhelming to me, so I might need some time to feel comfortable. But underneath my cautious exterior is a sweet little girl who is just waiting to learn that she’s safe and loved. I’m looking for a patient person who will let me take things at my own pace. I may not immediately jump into your lap or ask for attention, but with kindness, gentle encouragement, and a little time, I’m sure I’ll become more confident and let my personality shine. My dream is to find a loving home where I can feel safe, cozy, and cared for while I continue to grow. If you’re willing to give me the time I need, I promise that earning my trust will make our friendship all the more special. I can’t wait to find someone who will see the sweet girl behind my shyness! If you’re interested in adopting or fostering me, you can call 704-266-3647 or email NCteam@austinpetsalive.org to learn more.

memos.text: Hi, I’m Blair. I’m a 1-year-old gray tabby girl with a shy, gentle soul. New places and faces can feel a little overwhelming for me at first, so I might take some time to come out of my shell—but I promise I’m worth the wait. austin.name: Blink
austin.websiteMemo:
Meet Blink, a petite Lab mix with a gentle heart and a sweet, soulful personality. She may be a little shy when you first meet her, but give her a little time and she warms up quickly, showing just how affectionate and loving she truly is.

Blink is a wonderful companion who enjoys being near her people and would happily spend her days by your side, whether that’s relaxing at home or joining you for a stroll. She does great in an apartment setting and is already crate trained, making her an easy addition to many types of homes.

She gets along well with cats and has done well around other dogs, though she can be a bit shy and tends to prefer human company over rough-and-tumble play. Blink would thrive in a home that can offer her patience, reassurance, and lots of love as she continues to build her confidence.

Blink is currently located at our Elgin Transport Hub. Please email transporthub@austinpetsalive.org if you have any questions or would like to meet her!

austin.name: Blur
austin.websiteMemo: Have you ever seen a pup fight so hard just to share her immense love with the world? Blur is a remarkable parvo survivor who beat the odds, showcasing an inspiring, resilient spirit that fills every room with pure inspiration. With a pristine, snow-white coat, captivating almond-shaped eyes, and perfectly folded ears that frame her sweet face, she is an absolute head-turner. This brilliant girl is a master of the post-nap stretch, engaging in clumsy, light-footed lunges whenever she spots her favorite toys. Her sharp mind makes her an eager learner who thrives on affectionate praise, gentle playtime, and discovering new sights with quiet curiosity.Don't wait—make your move today to bring Blur home.

austin.name: Brook
austin.websiteMemo:
Hi, I'm Brook!!  💖

I'm a curious little lady who loves being right in the middle of the fun. I've had a blast playing with my two foster doggy brothers, wrestling with them and chasing them, and keeping up with them even though I'm not quite as fast or big! And I even give the kitties plenty of space to do their thing. But most of all, I love snuggling!! I've learned the art of belly rubs, and there's nothing I love more than curling up at my foster's feet between cuddle sessions. 

My story started when my siblings and I were found in the middle of a street, with no mama in sight. Thanks to some super kind humans, I’m safe now and ready for all the love and adventures the world has to offer.

I’m ready to learn and explore with my adoptive family. If you’re looking for a pup who’s playful, affectionate, and always up for snuggles, I’d love to meet you! 🐾

memos.text: This Addendum supplements your Adoption Contract with Austin Pets Alive! and outlines your obligations regarding the spay/neuter of your adopted pet. 1. Veterinary Care and Spay/Neuter Requirement I understand and agree to the following: (a) If my adopted pet has been released to me before being spayed or neutered, I agree to have the surgery completed within 90 days of the adoption date (b) I will follow veterinary guidelines to ensure my pet is fully vaccinated and protected from common diseases. (c) I understand that I am responsible for managing, training, and socializing my pet to develop appropriate behavior. 2. Spay/Neuter Scheduling Options Within two weeks of adoption, Shelter Pet Adoption Center staff will contact me by phone or email to schedule a spay/neuter appointment with one of Austin Pets Alive!’s veterinary partners. (a) If I choose this option, Austin Pets Alive! will cover the cost of the surgery and required medications directly related to that procedure. (b) I understand that any additional services (vaccinations, elective procedures, or other treatments) will be my financial responsibility. (c) Post-surgery complications due to non-compliance as decided by Austin Pets Alive! will be my responsibility 3. Using a Private Veterinarian I may choose to schedule the surgery with my own licensed veterinarian. In that case, I am responsible for all related costs. Proof of spay/neuter (such as a veterinary invoice or certificate) must be submitted to NCteam@austinpetsalive.org within 90 days of adoption. 4. Compliance Failure to provide proof of spay/neuter within 90 days may result in follow-up contact from Austin Pets Alive! and may be considered a breach of the adoption contract. A Friendly Note: You are not required to use your own vet, but doing so helps stretch our limited nonprofit resources and allows us to save more pets in need. Every time an adopter covers this cost, it helps us reach another animal waiting for help. memos.label: Disclaimer
memos.text:
I understand and agree as follows:
Full ownership of the animal described in this contract (“Animal”) will be transferred to me only after the medical treatment outlined in the contract disclaimers has been completed either at Austin Pets Alive, Inc. (“APA!”) or through a private veterinarian.
Until the adoption is complete:
(1) the Animal remains the property of APA!;
(2) APA! maintains responsibility only for the Animal’s Pre-Adopt Medical Treatment as outlined in this contract;
(3) I have assumed and am responsible for all medical treatment related to the Animal other than the Animal’s Pre-Adopt Medical Treatment as outlined in this contract;
(4) APA! has full authority to make decisions related to the Pre-Adopt Medical Treatment for the Animal;
(5) APA! can only provide medical care and create treatment plans that are financially reasonable and responsible for the organization;
(6) APA! cannot provide heroic care for patients suffering from chronic or terminal diseases. End-of-life decisions are made based on quality of life weighed against what would be considered reasonable care for APA! to provide this pet;
(7) APA! may take back the Animal at any time and for any reason;
(8) I must return the Animal to APA! within 24 hours of request/demand;
(9) I must notify APA! if the Animal sustains a life-threatening injury or illness; and
(10) APA! must be notified of any euthanasia recommendation by a private veterinarian before the Animal is euthanized, unless the recommendation is made after 7:00 pm or before 10:00 am and is based on an emergency.
All private veterinary expenses (including emergency services), whether incurred while the Animal is in Pre-Adopt status or after the Animal’s adoption is finalized, are my responsibility and that I will not be reimbursed by APA! for any such expenses, unless specifically provided otherwise in this Agreement.
I must comply with the Animal’s treatment plan and be proactive in the treatment and recovery of the Animal. If I am not, I understand that APA! may take the Animal back and cancel this adoption. I understand that if refuse to surrender the Animal to APA!, as required herein, APA! may outcome the animal as “Lost/Stolen” and/or pursue any and all available legal remedies against me.
Long-term follow-up and care will be my responsibility and APA! will not be liable for complications.

memos.label: Disclaimer
memos.text: This Addendum supplements your Adoption Contract with Austin Pets Alive! and outlines your obligations regarding the spay/neuter of your adopted pet. 1. Veterinary Care and Spay/Neuter Requirement I understand and agree to the following: (a) If my adopted pet has been released to me before being spayed or neutered, I agree to have the surgery completed within 90 days of the adoption date (b) I will follow veterinary guidelines to ensure my pet is fully vaccinated and protected from common diseases. (c) I understand that I am responsible for managing, training, and socializing my pet to develop appropriate behavior. 2. Spay/Neuter Scheduling Options Within two weeks of adoption, Shelter Pet Adoption Center staff will contact me by phone or email to schedule a spay/neuter appointment with one of Austin Pets Alive!’s veterinary partners. (a) If I choose this option, Austin Pets Alive! will cover the cost of the surgery and required medications directly related to that procedure. (b) I understand that any additional services (vaccinations, elective procedures, or other treatments) will be my financial responsibility. (c) Post-surgery complications due to non-compliance as decided by Austin Pets Alive! will be my responsibility 3. Using a Private Veterinarian I may choose to schedule the surgery with my own licensed veterinarian. In that case, I am responsible for all related costs. Proof of spay/neuter (such as a veterinary invoice or certificate) must be submitted to NCteam@austinpetsalive.org within 90 days of adoption. 4. Compliance Failure to provide proof of spay/neuter within 90 days may result in follow-up contact from Austin Pets Alive! and may be considered a breach of the adoption contract. A Friendly Note: You are not required to use your own vet, but doing so helps stretch our limited nonprofit resources and allows us to save more pets in need. Every time an adopter covers this cost, it helps us reach another animal waiting for help. Adopter Acknowledgment By signing the adoption contract, I acknowledge that I have read, understand, and agree to the terms of this Spay/Neuter Addendum.

I am currently at our Elgin Transport Hub. If you're interested in scheduling a meet-and-greet, please email us at transporthub@austinpetsalive.org.

memos.label: Disclaimer
memos.text: This Addendum supplements your Adoption Contract with Austin Pets Alive! and outlines your obligations regarding the spay/neuter of your adopted pet. 1. Veterinary Care and Spay/Neuter Requirement I understand and agree to the following: (a) If my adopted pet has been released to me before being spayed or neutered, I agree to have the surgery completed within 90 days of the adoption date (b) I will follow veterinary guidelines to ensure my pet is fully vaccinated and protected from common diseases. (c) I understand that I am responsible for managing, training, and socializing my pet to develop appropriate behavior. 2. Spay/Neuter Scheduling Options Within two weeks of adoption, Shelter Pet Adoption Center staff will contact me by phone or email to schedule a spay/neuter appointment with one of Austin Pets Alive!’s veterinary partners. (a) If I choose this option, Austin Pets Alive! will cover the cost of the surgery and required medications directly related to that procedure. (b) I understand that any additional services (vaccinations, elective procedures, or other treatments) will be my financial responsibility. (c) Post-surgery complications due to non-compliance as decided by Austin Pets Alive! will be my responsibility 3. Using a Private Veterinarian I may choose to schedule the surgery with my own licensed veterinarian. In that case, I am responsible for all related costs. Proof of spay/neuter (such as a veterinary invoice or certificate) must be submitted to NCteam@austinpetsalive.org within 90 days of adoption. 4. Compliance Failure to provide proof of spay/neuter within 90 days may result in follow-up contact from Austin Pets Alive! and may be considered a breach of the adoption contract. A Friendly Note: You are not required to use your own vet, but doing so helps stretch our limited nonprofit resources and allows us to save more pets in need. Every time an adopter covers this cost, it helps us reach another animal waiting for help. Adopter Acknowledgment By signing the adoption contract, I acknowledge that I have read, understand, and agree to the terms of this Spay/Neuter Addendum.

memos.text: Hi there! My name is Doug, and I'm a 2-month-old kitten with a big heart and an even bigger sense of adventure. I spend my days exploring, playing with toys, chasing imaginary creatures, and perfecting my zoomies around the house. I'm a curious little guy who loves discovering new things and meeting new friends. When I'm not busy playing, I enjoy snuggling up for naps in warm, cozy spots and soaking up all the love and attention I can get. I'm sweet, playful, and full of kitten energy. Whether I'm making you laugh with my silly antics or curling up beside you for a cuddle, I'm always ready to brighten your day. I may be tiny now, but I have a huge personality and so much love to share. I can't wait to find my forever family and start our adventures together! If you’re interested in adopting or fostering me, you can call 704-266-3647 or email NCteam@austinpetsalive.org to learn more.

memos.label: Kennel Card / Bio
memos.text: Hi, I’m Dove, a sweet 1-year-old girl who’s ready to spread my wings and find my forever home! I’m young, curious, and full of personality. I love having a cozy place to relax, soaking up attention, and enjoying all the little things that make life wonderful. I’m hoping for a loving family who will give me time to settle in and show them just how special I am. I may be petite, but I have a whole lot of love to give! I’m ready for new adventures, cozy naps, and plenty of happy moments with my people. Could you be the one I’ve been waiting for? If you’re interested in adopting or fostering me, you can call 704-266-3647 or email NCteam@austinpetsalive.org to learn more.

memos.label: Kennel Card / Bio
memos.text: Hi, I'm Draco! I'm a 9-week-old German Shepherd/Lab mix puppy with a big heart and an even bigger love for people. If you're looking for a sweet, cuddly sidekick, I might just be your perfect match! I love being close to my humans and am happiest when I'm soaking up attention, giving kisses, or curling up beside you for a nap. I'm a gentle, affectionate boy who enjoys making new friends and spreading puppy joy wherever I go. I'm also already showing off what a smart pup I am! I've been doing great with crate training and am learning that my crate is a cozy, safe place to relax and sleep. At my young age, that's pretty impressive, and I'm excited to keep learning all kinds of new things with my future family. Like any puppy, I'll need continued training, patience, and plenty of playtime as I grow, but I promise to repay you with endless love, loyalty, and lots of tail wags. If you're ready for a loving best friend who is off to a fantastic start and eager to be part of a family, come meet me! I can't wait to find my forever home. My adoption includes neuter surgery, age-appropriate vaccinations, a microchip, and a lifetime of puppy snuggles. Could I be the missing piece in your family? If you are interested in fostering or adopting me, please email NCteam@austinpetsalive.org or call (704) 266-3647.

I can be a little timid when I meet new people or find myself in unfamiliar places, but once I start to feel safe, my sweet personality begins to shine. Once I've built up my confidence, I'm happy to join in the fun and soak up affection from the people I trust. I'm hoping to find a forever home where I'll be given the time I need to adjust and blossom into the confident, loving cat I'm meant to be. If you're looking for a loyal little friend who will reward your patience with purrs, companionship, and lots of love, I just might be the perfect match. If you’re interested in adopting or fostering me, you can call 704-266-3647 or email NCteam@austinpetsalive.org to learn more.

I’m curious about everything around me, and I love exploring new spaces, investigating little sounds, and discovering all the fun things the world has to offer. Every day feels like an adventure, and I’m always ready for more. I’m a playful little guy who enjoys chasing toys, pouncing on anything that wiggles, and zooming around when I get the zoomies. memos.text: Hi, I’m Dwight—and yes, I’m as charming as my name suggests! I’m a 1.5-year-old orange kitty with a big personality and an even bigger heart. I’ve got that classic orange-cat energy: playful, curious, and just a little bit goofy. Whether I’m chasing toys, exploring every corner, or soaking up attention, I like to keep life interesting. memos.label: Kennel Card / Bio
memos.text: Meet Elias! Elias is a 6-month-old sweetheart who is quickly learning just how good life can be. He is a true human shadow and loves nothing more than being close to his people. Elias is happiest when he’s part of whatever his family is doing. As he settles into foster life, his playful puppy personality is starting to shine more and more. He is generally low to medium energy, walks well on a leash, is potty trained and crate trained, and has done well with both children and cats. Elias also enjoys other dogs, although he is still learning appropriate puppy manners. He can sometimes get overly excited during interactions and nip at another dog’s skin in an attempt to engage, so he’ll benefit from a family who can continue helping him learn how to play appropriately and respect other dogs’ boundaries. More than anything, Elias is incredibly sweet. Each day, he seems a little more comfortable trusting the people around him and realizing that humans can be kind, patient, and safe. His tail is wagging more and more every day, and watching his confidence grow has been such a special treat. Elias would love a home where he can continue learning, spend plenty of time with his people, and finally have a family to shadow. If you’re interested in adopting or fostering me, you can call 704-266-3647 or email NCteam@austinpetsalive.org to learn more.

memos.label: Kennel Card / Bio
memos.text: Meet Elie! If you're looking for a puppy who's equal parts adorable, playful, and affectionate, Elie is ready to steal your heart! This 5-month-old Husky mix weighs just 13 pounds, making her the perfect compact adventure buddy with plenty of growing left to do. Like any puppy, Elie is curious about the world and loves exploring, playing with toys, and making new friends. She's always up for a game, followed by plenty of snuggles when it's time to recharge. Her sweet personality and happy spirit make her a joy to be around. Elie is at the perfect age to continue learning all the important puppy basics. With positive training, consistency, and lots of love, she'll grow into a wonderful lifelong companion. Whether you're looking for a hiking partner, a playmate, or a cuddle buddy, Alina is excited to be by your side through it all. If you're ready to welcome a fun-loving, affectionate puppy into your family, Elie can't wait to meet you! If you’re interested in adopting or fostering her, you can call 704-266-3647 or email NCteam@austinpetsalive.org to learn more.

At first glance, she looks like a sleek black kitty, but when she steps into the sunlight, her secret is revealed: she is actually a gorgeous, deep dark chocolate brown with rich amber-red undertones. (8) I must return the Animal to APA! within 24 hours of request/demand;
(9) I must notify APA! if the Animal sustains a life-threatening injury or illness; and
(10) APA! must be notified of any euthanasia recommendation by a private veterinarian before the Animal is euthanized, unless the recommendation is made after 7:00 pm or before 10:00 am and is based on an emergency.
All private veterinary expenses (including emergency services), whether incurred while the Animal is in Pre-Adopt status or after the Animal’s adoption is finalized, are my responsibility and that I will not be reimbursed by APA! for any such expenses, unless specifically provided otherwise in this Agreement.

Veterinary Care and Spay/Neuter Requirement I understand and agree to the following: (a) If my adopted pet has been released to me before being spayed or neutered, I agree to have the surgery completed within 90 days of the adoption date (b) I will follow veterinary guidelines to ensure my pet is fully vaccinated and protected from common diseases. (c) I understand that I am responsible for managing, training, and socializing my pet to develop appropriate behavior. 2. Spay/Neuter Scheduling Options Within two weeks of adoption, Shelter Pet Adoption Center staff will contact me by phone or email to schedule a spay/neuter appointment with one of Austin Pets Alive!’s veterinary partners. (a) If I choose this option, Austin Pets Alive! will cover the cost of the surgery and required medications directly related to that procedure. (b) I understand that any additional services (vaccinations, elective procedures, or other treatments) will be my financial responsibility. (c) Post-surgery complications due to non-compliance as decided by Austin Pets Alive! will be my responsibility 3. Using a Private Veterinarian I may choose to schedule the surgery with my own licensed veterinarian. In that case, I am responsible for all related costs. Proof of spay/neuter (such as a veterinary invoice or certificate) must be submitted to NCteam@austinpetsalive.org within 90 days of adoption. 4. Compliance Failure to provide proof of spay/neuter within 90 days may result in follow-up contact from Austin Pets Alive! and may be considered a breach of the adoption contract. A Friendly Note: You are not required to use your own vet, but doing so helps stretch our limited nonprofit resources and allows us to save more pets in need. Every time an adopter covers this cost, it helps us reach another animal waiting for help. Adopter Acknowledgment By signing the adoption contract, I acknowledge that I have read, understand, and agree to the terms of this Spay/Neuter Addendum.

memos.label: Return
memos.text: From owner who returned him-"I would be happy to help. Yeah since in my home he only came to me. I worked with him to walk on a leash and he was still hesitant and nervous. If he ever saw another person not in my home he was anxious. He is also afraid of coming up the stairs. I tried positive reinforcement. I would use treats and praise when he took a step up. I have my service dog. He is 4 and he is a golden retriever. They were best friends until about 3 months ago. They were all here before Koda. I also have 2 older Poms. He would always go my younger Pom. So Gizmo would hide. My oldest Teddy is 10yrs old and she let him know hey don’t mess with me. So he left her alone after a couple weeks of times Teddy nipped at him. Shes a grouchy old lady. Now with my service dog. I would let them out together and get them each equal things. I know that doesn’t make a difference with some dogs. They are like little kids always wanting what the other has. Lol I am not sure what started the fight…but I see Koda and Obi fully biting at each other. Idk why there were no toys or treats out at the time. My husband had to pull them apart a couple times. We were hoping to have it sorted out because Koda was starting to respond better with me. They both slept in their kennels at night. Fed at the same time and same room. He loves playing with his toys and he loves his treats and getting lots of pets. I would invite him up on the couch  and give him belly rubs. He was skittish around people he didn’t see every day. He was a bit afraid of my sister in laws cat…but she can be a witch sometimes. She was also adopted from Petco. I hate that I had to give him back. He is such a sweet dog. Scared and anxious…but he is by no means a bad dog. I think he needs a family who can give him more one on one attention than I could. He was always anxious or scared. He loves playing fetch when his brain slows down enough to say oh that’s what we are playing. He picks up on things pretty quick. It took me 30mins to get him to sit stay and wait until his food was ready and his water was poured. Then I would release him by saying ok and same thing when I let him out of his kennel. I would ask him to sit and wait before I opened the door." They refused to get him neutered despite lots of follow up from our team. The owner said he was going after her resident dogs and that's pretty much all the information I could get. She refused to talk on the phone. He never received vet care after adoption. She said he was good with dogs at the dog park but not in her home. He pancakes on leash and I finally had to carry him to a kennel last night and he expressed his anal glands everywhere he was so scared. Vol. Katherine and her husband sat with him for an hour on 10/16, 10/17, and may come 10/18 and it took a minute for him to warm up, but eventually they got him playing with his ball, giving kisses, and eating treats.

memos.label: Medical
memos.text: Put on trazodone and gabapentin. Noticed potential gait abnormality in back legs. Please note weight is an estimate as we were not able to get him on a scale.

memos.label: Behavioral
memos.text: Staff are now able to walk him without an additional staff member present. He is a big chewer and does well with a benebone or other hard chew toy. He will chew up and ingest soft toys

memos.text:
From NC location: "We are seeking assistance with Lasagna, a 6-month-old Cattle Dog/Shepherd mix who arrived at our facility on 9/10/26.

When he first arrived, Lasagna was very shut down. He had little interest in eating, was terrified of the leash, and spent most of the day curled up in one spot. Since entering foster care, he has made great progress socially and behaviorally. He is eating more, gaining weight, and doing well on walks.

However, his foster is having difficulty with potty training. He has not made progress with pottying outside and is still using pads. His foster believes the leash may be contributing as he seems more interested in running around and sniffing now that he is feeling more comfortable. She would appreciate any guidance or recommendations for helping him transition to pottying outside while on leash."

Sent potty training guide and personal tips, and scared dog handout. JA

memos.label: Kennel Card / Bio
memos.text: Hiya mate! I am "Lottie". British slang for my big beauties, my EARS. I am 1 year old Rat Terrier/ Chihuahua and weigh in at a full feather load of 12 lbs. I recently went to stay with my Foster Ma & Pa and let me tell you, they are in aw of how much of a good girl I really am. Transition period? No way! I'm a lady and act like I've lived here my whole life. I am not a yapper at all...but will do a lil' "bruff-bruff" under my breath when I see someone new. But, as soon as they start my way for a pat and a smile, I am so ready to call you friend! I am cool to noises and such, nothing bothers or startles me at all. I am not a chewer of your items or a hyper lady, but I do like an occasional zoomie. No worries though, chill is my middle name. So chill, to the point where when I fell asleep on my mom's lap watching TV. I love walks & hopping through the yard. Not much for toys or balls, but I love & live to jump for little bugs. Ma says I look like a little Bambi fawn playing & hopping in the yard. Now, when I am inside, I am my Ma's shadow. Just happy to be wherever she is. Quiet as a mouse. Happy to be picked up, on your lap or just sitting quietly next to you. I get crated at night & I didn't make a peep until my Ma gets up. Oh, and I also use a pee pad or go outside. She says I am the perfect lady and from what she sees, I came to the Shelter at no fault of my own. I am looking for my forever home, and it will be like I haven't missed a beat. Fun fact: I am not only super chill in the car, but boats too! This summer vacation rocks! If you’re interested in adopting or fostering me, you can call 704-266-3647 or email NCteam@austinpetsalive.org to learn more.

memos.label: Internal (Private)
memos.text: Hi, I'm Lottie! The first thing you'll probably notice about me is my HUGE ears—they're pretty spectacular, if I do say so myself! They give me loads of personality and make everyone who meets me smile. I'm a 1-year-old Chihuahua mix with a heart that's every bit as big as my ears. I'm incredibly sweet, affectionate, and absolutely love being around people. Whether I'm curled up in your lap, following you from room to room, or happily accepting belly rubs, I'm happiest when I'm spending time with my favorite humans. I'm still young, so I enjoy exploring the world and going on adventures, but I also know how to slow down and enjoy a cozy cuddle on the couch. My loving personality and gentle nature make me an easy companion who's ready to become someone's very best friend. If you're looking for a loyal little shadow with an adorable face, unforgettable ears, and endless love to give, I just might be your perfect match. If you think I could be the one for you, please submit an adoption application. I can't wait to meet you and show you just how much love can fit into one little Chihuahua mix with the biggest ears around!

My calm personality makes me a wonderful match for just about any home that's ready for all the fun (and responsibility!) that comes with raising a puppy. If you're looking for a puppy with a gentle soul, a loving heart, and endless cuddles to give, I just might be your perfect match. memos.label: Kennel Card / Bio
memos.text: Hi, I'm Molly! I'm a 2-year-old Black Lab mix weighing 76 pounds, and while I may be a little shy at first, my foster family says my personality blossoms a little more every single day. When I first arrived, I was nervous about the world around me, but I'm gaining confidence and learning that new people can be wonderful. In fact, when my foster family's friend came over recently, I walked right up to say hello with a wagging tail! I still appreciate a gentle introduction, but once I know you're kind, I'm all in. I'm a girl with some adorable quirks! I take squirrel patrol very seriously and have convinced myself that if I walk slowly enough, they won't notice a 76-pound dog sneaking up on them. (Spoiler alert: they always do.) I also love lounging outside in the sunshine with my foster dog sibling and enjoy peaceful walks, especially as I continue building confidence around loud traffic. If you're taking a shower, don't worry—I'll be stationed just outside the bathroom to make sure you're safe. It's a big responsibility, but someone has to do it! And when it's time to relax, nothing makes me happier than cuddling on the couch. I'll carefully sneak up one paw at a time until I'm curled up as close to you as possible. I'm convinced I'm being incredibly stealthy...even if my foster family says otherwise. I'm also the total package: potty trained, crate trained, and well-mannered around the house. And don't forget to watch for my adorable smile—sometimes my lips get caught on my teeth, giving me the cutest goofy grin that will melt your heart. If you’re interested in adopting or fostering me, you can call 704-266-3647 or email NCteam@austinpetsalive.org to learn more.

memos.label: Kennel Card / Bio
memos.text: Hi there! I’m Nellie — your future best friend in a perfectly pocket-sized package. At just 32 pounds, I’m basically a “carry-me-if-you-want-to (but I can totally walk myself)” kind of girl. I’m 7 months old, which means I’ve got that fun, playful puppy energy without being too over-the-top. I’m a total dream on leash — I walk calmly right by your side, happy to take in the world with you. Whether it’s neighborhood strolls or weekend adventures, I’m your easygoing companion. I’m also very food-motivated (treats = love language), which makes me a great student if you want to teach me new tricks! I absolutely adore kids and would love a family where I can soak up all the attention and affection. I also get along well with other dogs, so I’d be happy to have a canine sibling or two to play with. If you’re looking for a sweet, well-mannered, fun-sized pup who fits perfectly into just about any home, I think we might be meant to be. Come meet me — I’ll be the one wagging my tail and ready to win you over. If you’re interested in adopting or fostering me, you can call 704-266-3647 or email NCteam@austinpetsalive.org to learn more.

memos.label: Kennel Card / Bio
memos.text: Hi! I'm Nellie, but everyone calls me Nervous Nellie because I can be a little timid when I first meet new people or find myself in new situations. I'm a 9-week-old German Shepherd/Lab mix puppy with a gentle heart that's just waiting for the right family to help it bloom. I may be shy, but I take comfort in having doggy friends around and absolutely love other dogs. They help me feel brave and show me that the world isn't such a scary place after all! Once I feel safe, you'll see my sweet, playful side start to shine. I also have a not-so-secret obsession: water! Kiddie pools, sprinklers, puddles—you name it, I'm ready to splash around and have some fun. Water seems to bring out my confidence and reminds me that being a puppy is supposed to be exciting. Because I'm still learning that people can be kind and new experiences can be fun, I'll do best with a patient family willing to let me move at my own pace. Another friendly dog in the home would be a huge bonus and could help me continue building confidence. If you're looking for a gentle soul to nurture and watch blossom into a loving companion, I just might be your girl. I promise that earning my trust will be rewarded with a lifetime of loyalty, sweet snuggles, and plenty of splashes along the way! My adoption includes spay surgery, age-appropriate vaccinations, a microchip, and lots of puppy kisses. Come meet me and see if we're meant to help each other grow! I'm on the lookout for a family who's ready to watch me grow into who I'm meant to be. Could that be you? If you are interested in fostering or adopting me, please email NCteam@austinpetsalive.org or call (704) 266-3647.

Full ownership of the animal described in this contract (“Animal”) will be transferred to me only after the medical treatment outlined in the contract disclaimers has been completed either at Austin Pets Alive, Inc. (“APA!”) or through a private veterinarian.

(2) APA! maintains responsibility only for the Animal’s Pre-Adopt Medical Treatment as outlined in this contract;
(3) I have assumed and am responsible for all medical treatment related to the Animal other than the Animal’s Pre-Adopt Medical Treatment as outlined in this contract;
(4) APA! has full authority to make decisions related to the Pre-Adopt Medical Treatment for the Animal;
(5) APA! can only provide medical care and create treatment plans that are financially reasonable and responsible for the organization;
(6) APA! cannot provide heroic care for patients suffering from chronic or terminal diseases. End-of-life decisions are made based on quality of life weighed against what would be considered reasonable care for APA! to provide this pet;
(7) APA! may take back the Animal at any time and for any reason;
(8) I must return the Animal to APA! within 24 hours of request/demand;
(9) I must notify APA! if the Animal sustains a life-threatening injury or illness; and
(10) APA! must be notified of any euthanasia recommendation by a private veterinarian before the Animal is euthanized, unless the recommendation is made after 7:00 pm or before 10:00 am and is based on an emergency.
All private veterinary expenses (including emergency services), whether incurred while the Animal is in Pre-Adopt status or after the Animal’s adoption is finalized, are my responsibility and that I will not be reimbursed by APA! for any such expenses, unless specifically provided otherwise in this Agreement.
I must comply with the Animal’s treatment plan and be proactive in the treatment and recovery of the Animal. If I am not, I understand that APA! may take the Animal back and cancel this adoption. I understand that if refuse to surrender the Animal to APA!, as required herein, APA! may outcome the animal as “Lost/Stolen” and/or pursue any and all available legal remedies against me.

memos.label: Disclaimer
memos.text:
I understand and agree as follows:
Full ownership of the animal described in this contract (“Animal”) will be transferred to me only after the medical treatment outlined in the contract disclaimers has been completed either at Austin Pets Alive, Inc. (“APA!”) or through a private veterinarian.
Until the adoption is complete:
(1) the Animal remains the property of APA!;
(2) APA! maintains responsibility only for the Animal’s Pre-Adopt Medical Treatment as outlined in this contract;
(3) I have assumed and am responsible for all medical treatment related to the Animal other than the Animal’s Pre-Adopt Medical Treatment as outlined in this contract;
(4) APA! has full authority to make decisions related to the Pre-Adopt Medical Treatment for the Animal;
(5) APA! can only provide medical care and create treatment plans that are financially reasonable and responsible for the organization;
(6) APA! cannot provide heroic care for patients suffering from chronic or terminal diseases. End-of-life decisions are made based on quality of life weighed against what would be considered reasonable care for APA! to provide this pet;
(7) APA! may take back the Animal at any time and for any reason;
(8) I must return the Animal to APA! within 24 hours of request/demand;
(9) I must notify APA! if the Animal sustains a life-threatening injury or illness; and
(10) APA! must be notified of any euthanasia recommendation by a private veterinarian before the Animal is euthanized, unless the recommendation is made after 7:00 pm or before 10:00 am and is based on an emergency.
All private veterinary expenses (including emergency services), whether incurred while the Animal is in Pre-Adopt status or after the Animal’s adoption is finalized, are my responsibility and that I will not be reimbursed by APA! for any such expenses, unless specifically provided otherwise in this Agreement.
I must comply with the Animal’s treatment plan and be proactive in the treatment and recovery of the Animal. If I am not, I understand that APA! may take the Animal back and cancel this adoption. I understand that if refuse to surrender the Animal to APA!, as required herein, APA! may outcome the animal as “Lost/Stolen” and/or pursue any and all available legal remedies against me.
Long-term follow-up and care will be my responsibility and APA! will not be liable for complications.

memos.label: Disclaimer
memos.text:
Return Policy - Animals Adopted at the Shelter Pet Adoption Center in North Carolina

I understand and agree as follows:

The policy for returning an Animal adopted from Austin Pets Alive! (APA!) through the Shelter Pet Adoption Center in North Carolina differs from the policy for Animals adopted from APA! in Austin, Texas. That policy is stated in my adoption contract under section 7 on Surrenders and is subject to this disclaimer:

If I am ever unable or unwilling to care for the Animal I have adopted, I understand that the following policy applies for Animals adopted through the Shelter Pet Adoption Center in North Carolina:

(1) The 30 days after the date of the adoption will be a grace period, when I will be permitted to return my Animal to the custody of Austin Pets Alive! in North Carolina.
(2) APA! will require that I reach out first to NCTeam@austinpetsalive.org for help in resolving any problems with my ability and willingness to care for the Animal, or
(3) I may transfer ownership of the Animal to a friend or family member willing and able to care for the Animal, and will in that case inform APA! of the name and contact information for the new owner.
(4) If I am still unable or unwilling to care for the Animal and am not able to transfer ownership, I will reach out to NCTeam@austinpetsalive.org to arrange for the Animal’s return.
(5) I understand that the timing of the return will depend on the availability of space and care capacity at the North Carolina center and that the return may be waitlisted; and I agree that I will continue to care for the Animal until the return.
(6) For return requests made more than 30 days after the Animal’s adoption, APA! reserves the right to decline surrender of the Animal to APA!’s custody, and will make any decision to accept the Animal’s return based on the organization’s capacity to care for the Animal and based on APA!’s judgement of the best interests of the Animal.
(7) APA! will first offer support in resolving any problems with my ability and willingness to care for the Animal and/or support in my efforts to rehome the Animal before it will agree to accept a return requested more than 30 days after adoption.

Veterinary Care and Spay/Neuter Requirement I understand and agree to the following: (a) If my adopted pet has been released to me before being spayed or neutered, I agree to have the surgery completed within 90 days of the adoption date (b) I will follow veterinary guidelines to ensure my pet is fully vaccinated and protected from common diseases. (c) I understand that I am responsible for managing, training, and socializing my pet to develop appropriate behavior. 2. Spay/Neuter Scheduling Options Within two weeks of adoption, Shelter Pet Adoption Center staff will contact me by phone or email to schedule a spay/neuter appointment with one of Austin Pets Alive!’s veterinary partners. (a) If I choose this option, Austin Pets Alive! will cover the cost of the surgery and required medications directly related to that procedure. (b) I understand that any additional services (vaccinations, elective procedures, or other treatments) will be my financial responsibility. (c) Post-surgery complications due to non-compliance as decided by Austin Pets Alive! will be my responsibility 3. Using a Private Veterinarian I may choose to schedule the surgery with my own licensed veterinarian. In that case, I am responsible for all related costs. Proof of spay/neuter (such as a veterinary invoice or certificate) must be submitted to NCteam@austinpetsalive.org within 90 days of adoption. 4. Compliance Failure to provide proof of spay/neuter within 90 days may result in follow-up contact from Austin Pets Alive! and may be considered a breach of the adoption contract. A Friendly Note: You are not required to use your own vet, but doing so helps stretch our limited nonprofit resources and allows us to save more pets in need. Every time an adopter covers this cost, it helps us reach another animal waiting for help. Adopter Acknowledgment By signing the adoption contract, I acknowledge that I have read, understand, and agree to the terms of this Spay/Neuter Addendum.

austin.websiteMemo:
Looking for a little luck and a lot of love? Meet Red Envelope, a stunning all-black Labrador mix puppy with a heart of gold!

True to her name, this shy sweet girl is a total gift. With her soulful eyes and soft, velvet-black fur, she is as charming as he is cute. Red Envelope is a gentle soul who loves to curl up in cozy blankets and offers the best puppy snuggles you could ask for. Like any young Lab mix, she’s ready to learn, play, and grow into the loyal best friend you’ve been waiting for.

Red Envelope’s Wishlist:

- A cozy spot to nap (preferably right next to you!).
- Plenty of toys and treats for a growing girl.
- A patient family ready to guide her through all her puppy milestones.

Bring some extra fortune into your home—adopt Red Envelope today!

memos.label: Disclaimer
memos.text:
I understand and agree as follows:
Full ownership of the animal described in this contract (“Animal”) will be transferred to me only after the medical treatment outlined in the contract disclaimers has been completed either at Austin Pets Alive, Inc. (“APA!”) or through a private veterinarian.
Until the adoption is complete:
(1) the Animal remains the property of APA!;
(2) APA! maintains responsibility only for the Animal’s Pre-Adopt Medical Treatment as outlined in this contract;
(3) I have assumed and am responsible for all medical treatment related to the Animal other than the Animal’s Pre-Adopt Medical Treatment as outlined in this contract;
(4) APA! has full authority to make decisions related to the Pre-Adopt Medical Treatment for the Animal;
(5) APA! can only provide medical care and create treatment plans that are financially reasonable and responsible for the organization;
(6) APA! cannot provide heroic care for patients suffering from chronic or terminal diseases. End-of-life decisions are made based on quality of life weighed against what would be considered reasonable care for APA! to provide this pet;
(7) APA! may take back the Animal at any time and for any reason;
(8) I must return the Animal to APA! within 24 hours of request/demand;
(9) I must notify APA! if the Animal sustains a life-threatening injury or illness; and
(10) APA! must be notified of any euthanasia recommendation by a private veterinarian before the Animal is euthanized, unless the recommendation is made after 7:00 pm or before 10:00 am and is based on an emergency.
All private veterinary expenses (including emergency services), whether incurred while the Animal is in Pre-Adopt status or after the Animal’s adoption is finalized, are my responsibility and that I will not be reimbursed by APA! for any such expenses, unless specifically provided otherwise in this Agreement.
I must comply with the Animal’s treatment plan and be proactive in the treatment and recovery of the Animal. If I am not, I understand that APA! may take the Animal back and cancel this adoption. I understand that if refuse to surrender the Animal to APA!, as required herein, APA! may outcome the animal as “Lost/Stolen” and/or pursue any and all available legal remedies against me.
Long-term follow-up and care will be my responsibility and APA! will not be liable for complications.

austin.name: Rugby
austin.websiteMemo:
Don’t let his tough-sounding name fool you—Rugby is a big, gentle sweetheart who is looking for a loving home where he can truly bloom!

Rugby can be a little shy when meeting new people or stepping into new environments, but with a few soft treats and a patient, gentle voice, his sweet, affectionate personality shines right through. Once he knows he’s safe, he’ll be your most loyal sidekick. He seems very dog-friendly and takes great comfort in having canine buddies around!

Rugby’s Highlights:

Sweet & Gentle: A quiet, loving boy who just wants to feel safe and adored.

Dog Friendly: Gets along well with other pups and enjoys doggy company.

Crate Trained: House-proud and does wonderfully in his crate for cozy naps and quiet time.

Working on Skills: Needs a patient human to help him practice his leash-walking skills (he's learning that walkies are fun, not scary!).

Rugby is currently located at our Elgin facility. If you are interested in meeting him, please email us at transporthub@austinpetsalive.org

memos.text: Ruh-roh! Have you seen the Mystery Machine? Scooby-Doo here, and I'm on the hunt for my very own Mystery Gang! At 2 years old, I've already mastered the art of sniffing out clues (and Scooby Snacks from miles away). My ears are so good, I can hear the dinner bell all the way from Spooky Island! Just call out, "Scooby-Doo, where are you?!" and I'll come running. Whether we're solving mysteries, going on adventures, or just hanging out like a couple of meddling kids, I'm always ready for fun. Ghosts? No problem! I may not walk on two legs, but I've got plenty of groovy moves to keep the good times rolling. I'm searching for my very own Shaggy—someone who'll be my best friend through every adventure. I'm just as happy spending the day lounging on the couch as I am helping you make the biggest sandwiches in the kitchen before hopping into the Mystery Machine for our next outing. austin.websiteMemo:
Sky is a beautiful calico lady with lots of personality and plenty to say about… well, just about everything! If you enjoy a good conversation, she’ll happily chat with you all day long. She likes to greet her people with cheerful meows and share her thoughts whenever something interesting happens.

She’s spent a decade perfecting the art of being a wonderful companion. She enjoys cozy spots, gentle pets, and being near people.

Her calico coat makes her look extra fancy, but deep down she’s just a sweet, talkative girl who wants a home where she can feel safe, loved, and heard. If you’re the kind of person who likes a cat with a big voice and an even bigger heart, she thinks you’ll get along just fine.

All APA! cats are fully vetted, spayed or neutered, and have updated vaccines and a microchip. Lifetime support is offered by our Cat Behavior Team.

For further information or to meet Sky, please email adopt@austinpetsalive.org.

austin.name: Tulip
austin.websiteMemo:
Affectionate, Playful, Big Purrs!

Tulip is a young girlie with a bright personality. She’s still young, so she’s got plenty of playful energy. She loves chasing toys, pouncing on anything that moves, and turning everyday moments into a game. 

Tulip will run right to you the minute you slide her door open; she's unabashed in her affection. She's confident and fun, and is as game to play as she is for pets. She loves her little fishies on a string and any soft toys. She's a roly-poly girl so expect to see her belly a lot. 

She’s a big fan of people. Once she gets to know you, she’ll happily come over for pets and attention, and she might even follow you around just to see what you’re up to. She’s got a sweet side, too. After playtime, she’s more than ready to curl up nearby and relax, hoping you pet her behind her ears! 

She’s curious about the world and excited to find a home where she can grow, play, and be loved. If you’re looking for a fun, affectionate companion with a little spark, she might just be your perfect match!

All APA! cats are fully vetted, spayed or neutered, and have updated vaccines and a microchip. Lifetime support is offered by our Cat Behavior Team.

For further information or to meet Tulip, please email adopt@austinpetsalive.org.

austin.websiteMemo:

Bringing a young dog into your life means enjoying those clumsy, heartwarming moments of growth while guiding them into a loyal companion.

Don't wait—make your move today to bring Violet home.

Full ownership of the animal described in this contract (“Animal”) will be transferred to me only after the medical treatment outlined in the contract disclaimers has been completed either at Austin Pets Alive, Inc. (“APA!”) or through a private veterinarian.

memos.label: Behavioral
memos.text:
Reported by: Adopter (Elizabeth Lauria)

Winston being returned to SPAC on 7/9 and going to Elgin due to space constraints in NC.

Summary of Reported Behaviors:

While training Winston not to get on the couch, the adopter gave the verbal cue "off" and reached toward his collar to guide him down. Winston snapped toward her hand. The adopter then attached a leash and was able to guide him off the couch without further incident. She reported that he responded appropriately when redirected with the leash.

On another occasion, Winston became highly focused on digging a hole in the yard. When the adopter attempted to interrupt the behavior, he growled and snapped at her.

The adopter stated that Winston was reportedly "aggressive" while playing with her daughter. She did not have additional details regarding this incident.

During an interaction with the adopter's niece's dog, Winston took possession of one of the other dog's toys and became possessive. The dogs were face-to-face with the toy positioned behind Winston. Winston growled and lunged toward the other dog. The other dog placed its front paws on Winston's back, but neither dog sustained bite injuries.

The final incident occurred when an air conditioning service technician arrived at the home. Winston initially growled at the individual at the front door. The adopter instructed Winston to go to his bed, and he complied. While the adopter escorted the technician through the house, Winston left his bed, approached the technician, and bit him on the leg. The bite ripped the technician's pants and caused bruising. The adopter noted that Winston's teeth are very worn down and believes he released immediately after making contact and ran away.

Additional Information:

-Winston is described as generally very sweet, enjoys sleeping on furniture, and seeks affection.
-Winston has a tendency to attempt to run out the front door if given the opportunity.
-He is comfortable being crated, sleeps in his crate overnight, and remains crated when the adopter is away from home.
-The adopter reports providing exercise through backyard time and regular walks.
-Winston frequently licks his paws, particularly when they are wet.
-He is possessive of tennis balls and is reluctant to relinquish them once he has them.
-According to a DNA test completed by the adopter, Winston is a mix of Miniature Schnauzer, Pitbull, and Cocker Spaniel.

memos.label: Kennel Card / Bio
memos.text: Hi, I’m Zami. I might seem a little shy when we first meet, and I like to take my time to feel out new people and places. I prefer to quietly observe at first, making sure everything feels safe and calm before I fully come out of my shell. Once I realize I can trust you, I really start to open up and show my sweet side. When I’m comfortable, I enjoy gentle affection and will happily lean in for pets and attention. I have a soft, loving personality that shines through more and more the longer we know each other. I’m the kind of cat who builds a strong bond with the people she trusts, and I truly appreciate kindness and patience. If you give me a chance, I think you’ll find I’m worth the wait. If you’re interested in adopting or fostering me, I’m available at 10017 Biddick Lane, Huntersville, NC 28078 inside Petco. You can call 704-266-3647 or email NCteam@austinpetsalive.org to learn more.
